name: Hypamoon Connect
author: hypamoon

sections.description:
Hypamoon Connect links your WordPress site to your Hypamoon project. It does two things.

Hypamoon on your site. Visitors get answers at night and in the weekend, and every message of your contact form lands in one place, with an email to you.

  • The chat window of your Hypamoon project on every page. The assistant of your project answers, with your own business name.
  • Contact forms that send their entries to your Hypamoon project, with an email for each entry, a bot check and a hidden spam trap. Add one to a page with the “Hypamoon form” block or a shortcode like [hypamoon_form id="contact"].
  • No code to paste. Ask your AI assistant connected to Hypamoon, for example “put the chat and a contact form on my WordPress site”, then open Tools > Hypamoon, Site tools. Or turn the chat on there yourself.
  • The chat and forms keep working when the connection of the plugin expires. Turn them off under Tools > Hypamoon.

Moving your data. Moving a site often stops at the login screen. Public pages are easy to copy, but drafts, private posts, form entries, orders and customers sit behind your WordPress login. Hypamoon Connect moves that data to your own Hypamoon project, without screenshots and without sharing a password in a chat.

You need a Hypamoon account to use this plugin. You can start with a free test project at https://app.hypamoon.com.

Two ways to work. Simple (the default for a new installation): the plugin only connects and shows what was sent; your chat with your AI assistant suggests what to move, asks you to confirm, and starts it. Full: every choice on this screen, with the suggestion of your chat shown on top so you can apply it. You can switch at any time; your selection stays.

How moving works:

  1. Create a one-time code in your Hypamoon project under Sites, or ask your AI assistant connected to Hypamoon for one.
  2. Enter the code under Tools > Hypamoon, Connection, and press Connect.
  3. The plugin sends an overview of your site: counts, dates and field names only, never content.
  4. Choose what moves: tell your chat what you want (for example “move my hours portal”) and it suggests a selection with a reason per kind of data; or choose in your Hypamoon project, or in WordPress under Move data. For every kind of data you see the number of items, example fields with their type, an estimated size, whether it holds personal data and why, the collection it goes to and the links that become references. Personal data stays off until you turn it on, also with Select all.
  5. Press Send. The data goes in small batches with a progress bar, so it works on shared hosting. If the connection drops, press Resume: nothing is sent twice.

What can move:

  • Posts, pages and public custom post types, including drafts, pending, private and scheduled items
  • Post types that are not public, like hours, applications or bookings of a member portal (off until you choose them, kept private)
  • Custom fields from Advanced Custom Fields, ACF Pro or Secure Custom Fields, in full: repeaters, flexible content, groups, images, relationships, plus field group definitions and options pages
  • Categories, tags and other terms
  • Media, as URLs only (files are not copied)
  • Menus
  • Form entries from Contact Form 7 (through Flamingo), WPForms and Gravity Forms
  • WooCommerce products and variations, orders with refunds and notes, customers, coupons, shipping zones, tax rates, product reviews and an overview of WooCommerce Subscriptions
  • Users: name, email and role, never passwords. With “All fields” also the other user fields, like a client id
  • Links between your data: a field that points to a user or a post (for example a client id on a timesheet) becomes a reference to that record in your project
  • Tables that a plugin or theme made in your database, with their columns (off until you choose them, kept private; WordPress core tables are never offered)
  • Settings from the options table that you tick one by one. Settings that look like a password, key or token are never listed and never sent

You can send again later. Records that were sent before are updated, never duplicated.

A WP-CLI command is included for large sites: wp hypamoon connect <code>, wp hypamoon status, wp hypamoon inventory, wp hypamoon selection, wp hypamoon export (with --dry-run, --include, --users and --restart) and wp hypamoon disconnect.

For developers: the filter hypamoon_connect_record lets you change or leave out a record before it is sent, hypamoon_connect_post_types changes the list of post types that are offered, hypamoon_connect_private_post_types and hypamoon_connect_tables narrow the post types that are not public and the database tables that are offered, and hypamoon_connect_show_chat decides per page view whether the chat window is shown (for example to wait for consent).

Privacy

Moving data. What is sent: only the data you select, plus an overview of your site (counts, oldest and newest dates, statuses, form field names and custom field definitions, never content). Personal data (form entries, orders, customers, subscriptions, reviews, users, post types that are not public and database tables of plugins) is off by default. Settings from the options table move only by name, when you tick them.

To whom: Hypamoon, the Netherlands, into your own Hypamoon project.

When: when an administrator presses Connect, Refresh inventory, Load latest selection, Save selection, Send, Apply suggestion and Save, Dismiss or Disconnect, or runs a WP-CLI command of this plugin. While the site is connected, a light check every five minutes (WP-Cron) asks Hypamoon whether you asked your chat to send your selection; only then is the selection sent, the one you confirmed in your chat or here. Hypamoon can start that check right away with a signed wake request without data. Personal data only goes when you said yes to it. Log, security and analytics tables, and tables with email or IP address columns, are never selected for you.

Where it goes: into collections in your own project, such as wp_posts, wp_pages, wp_media, wp_menus, wp_terms, wp_acf, wp_form_, wp_products, wp_orders, wp_customers, wp_shop_settings, wp_reviews, wp_subscriptions, wp_users, wp_table_ and wp_options. Collections with personal data are always private. Everything is private by default; the project owner decides what is published.

Clean-move check (since 1.5.0). Before Hypamoon moves your content, the plugin checks this site for signs of a known break-in: Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 (handed out as an infected copy on October 15 and 16, 2026) with the date of its files, the file wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php, the administrators, settings with program code in them and scheduled tasks that stand out. It only reads. What is sent: the version and dates, whether the file exists, per administrator the login, the domain of the email address (never the address) and the date the account was made, per setting that stands out only its name, length and the rule that matched (never its value), and per scheduled task that stands out only its name and owner. You see the same result under Tools > Hypamoon, Clean-move check, also without a connection. This is not a full malware scan.

Never sent: passwords, password hashes, sessions, keys and tokens, application passwords, post passwords and payment details. IP addresses and user agents only go along in a database table that you tick yourself.

Chat window and forms. When they are on your site, the browser of a visitor sends chat messages and form entries straight to your Hypamoon project, together with the address of the page and, as with any request, the IP address and browser of the visitor. Hypamoon uses them to answer, to store the entry, to email it to you, and to stop abuse with limits and a bot check (Cloudflare Turnstile). They go to Hypamoon, the Netherlands, as a processor for you. Your WordPress server sends nothing about visitors.

The plugin stores its connection details in the WordPress options table, without autoload, and the chat and form settings in one small option, also without autoload. Uninstalling the plugin deletes them.

Privacy policy: https://hypamoon.com/privacy
Terms: https://hypamoon.com/terms

External services

This plugin connects to the Hypamoon API (https://api.hypamoon.com), a service of Hypamoon, to move your data into your Hypamoon project.

  • When you press Connect, the one-time code, the site address, the site name, the WordPress version and the plugin version are sent, and an access token is received.
  • Right after connecting and when you press Refresh inventory, an overview of your site is sent: counts, dates, statuses, form field names, custom field definitions, the names of user fields and of meta fields of custom post types, the names and columns of database tables of plugins, and the names of settings (never their values), no content.
  • When you load or save the selection, the selection (which kinds of data, periods, statuses, fields to leave out, whether all fields go, and which settings) is read or written.
  • When you press Send or run wp hypamoon export, the data you selected is sent in batches.
  • When you press Disconnect, the access token is revoked.
  • When you open Move data, or the simple screen, the suggestion of your chat is read (which kinds of data, with a reason each) and whether your chat asked to send. When you apply and save it, or dismiss it, Hypamoon is told.
  • While the site is connected, WP-Cron checks every five minutes whether your chat asked to send your selection. If so, the selected data is sent in batches, for at most two minutes per check and always within the time limit of PHP. The check is removed when you disconnect or deactivate the plugin.
  • Wake route (since 1.4.2). Right after you confirm in your chat that your selection may be sent, Hypamoon (from api.hypamoon.com) sends a POST to https://your-site/?rest_route=/hypamoon-connect/v1/wake, so the check above runs at once instead of within five minutes. Why: without it, a site with few visitors can wait a long time for WP-Cron. The request holds no data and no token: only a timestamp, a random nonce and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over both, made with a key derived from the access token of your site. The plugin accepts it only with a valid signature, a clock at most five minutes apart and a nonce that was not used before, and at most 12 times per five minutes. It then plans the check (WP-Cron) and answers 202; the check itself sends only what you confirmed. If the route cannot be reached, nothing breaks: the five minute check picks the round up.
  • Clean-move check (since 1.5.0). Right after connecting, when you press Refresh inventory or Run the check, and at most every six hours during the five minute check, the result of the clean-move check is sent (see Privacy): versions, dates, logins with the domain of their email address, and names with rule codes. Never the content of a setting, a password or an email address.
  • When you open Tools > Hypamoon (at most once every five minutes), press Refresh, Turn chat on, Turn chat off or Set up forms, the chat and form settings for your site are read or changed: whether the chat is on, its colour, position, title and welcome text, the forms with their fields, and the public token of your project.

Every request from your WordPress server carries the access token and the address of your site. Apart from the five minute check above (or its wake), no request is made from your server without an action of an administrator, and none while other admin pages load.

The chat window and forms load scripts from the Hypamoon API in the browser of your visitors:

  • The chat window loads https://api.hypamoon.com/widget.js on every page while the chat is on. It reads the chat settings from Hypamoon, and sends the messages a visitor types to your Hypamoon project, where the assistant of your project answers.
  • A form loads https://api.hypamoon.com/form.js on the pages with a Hypamoon form. When a visitor sends the form, the fields are sent to your Hypamoon project.
  • Both show a bot check from Hypamoon in a small frame, which uses Cloudflare Turnstile. Cloudflare terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/ and privacy policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

These requests carry the public token of your project. It is public by design: it can only chat and add form entries, only from your site, with limits.

Terms of service: https://hypamoon.com/terms
Privacy policy: https://hypamoon.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin through Plugins > Add New, or upload the hypamoon-connect folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Tools > Hypamoon and enter the one-time code from your Hypamoon project on the Connection tab.
  4. For the chat and forms: ask your AI assistant to put them on your site, or press Turn chat on under Site tools. Add a form to a page with the “Hypamoon form” block.
sections.faq:
Is anything sent automatically?

Only after you connect the site. Your WordPress server then contacts Hypamoon when an administrator acts: Connect, Refresh inventory, Load latest selection, Save selection, Send, Disconnect, the chat and form buttons, or opening Tools > Hypamoon (which loads the latest chat and form settings, at most once every five minutes), or a WP-CLI command.

There is one scheduled task: while the site is connected, a light WP-Cron check every five minutes asks Hypamoon whether you asked your chat to send your selection. Only then is the selection sent, the one you confirmed in your chat or on this screen, and personal data only when you said yes to it. The check stops when you disconnect or deactivate the plugin. There is no tracking and no usage data is collected.

Right after you confirm in your chat that your selection may be sent, Hypamoon calls a small signed route on your site (wake) so the check runs at once instead of within five minutes. That request carries no data; see External services.

Does Select all send my logs?

No. Log, security and analytics tables (for example Wordfence, BlogVault and BulletProof tables starting with bv_, MainWP Stream, iThemes Security, Sucuri and activity logs, plus tables named like logs, sessions, transients or IP), and tables with email or IP address columns, are never ticked for you, also not with Select all and “Include personal data”. You can tick one yourself; Send then asks for an extra yes.

My chat chose what to move. What if I press Select all?

If what you send differs from what your chat chose, the screen asks first: “Your chat selected only: Users. Send that, or send your own selection?” The choice of your chat is the default.

When the chat window or a form is on your site, the browser of a visitor loads a script from Hypamoon and talks to Hypamoon directly. See External services.

Where do the answers of the chat come from?

From the assistant of your Hypamoon project: the same one that can answer your phone. You set what it knows and how it talks in your Hypamoon project or in your chat with your AI assistant. Without an assistant the chat has nothing to say, so set that up first.

Where do form entries go?

Into a collection of your Hypamoon project, and you get an email for each entry. A field named email becomes the reply address of that email. The form has a bot check (Cloudflare Turnstile, shown in a small frame from Hypamoon) and a hidden spam trap.

Does the chat need a cookie banner?

The chat window sets no cookies. It keeps the open conversation in the session storage of the browser until the tab is closed, and loads its settings from Hypamoon when the page loads, which sends the address of the visitor to Hypamoon like any other request. If your site waits for consent before loading services from others, use the filter hypamoon_connect_show_chat to show the chat only after consent. Mention Hypamoon in your privacy policy as a processor of chat messages and form entries.

Are passwords sent?

Never. User passwords, password hashes, sessions, activation keys, application passwords, post passwords and payment details are never sent. IP addresses and user agents only go along in a database table that you tick yourself. Meta keys, table columns and settings that look like a secret (password, token, key, nonce, hash, salt, auth) are left out. Meta keys that start with an underscore are only sent when you choose “All fields”, and never when they look like a secret.

Do the users get a password on Hypamoon?

No passwords move. When your Hypamoon project turns the users into users of an app, they sign in with a link or a code by email.

My Contact Form 7 entries are missing

Contact Form 7 does not store entries itself. Install Flamingo to keep entries from then on; the plugin reads them from there.

What happens with WooCommerce Subscriptions?

The overview moves: who is still subscribed, plan, amount, interval and next payment date. The recurring payments themselves do not move: they run at the payment provider and must be set up again. Hypamoon can help with paid access with an interval.

My hosting has short time limits. Will it work?

Yes. Every batch is a separate request of at most 200 records, so each request stays short. If a request fails, press Resume.

How do I disconnect?

Press Disconnect under Tools > Hypamoon, or run wp hypamoon disconnect. The access is revoked and the local settings for moving data are deleted. Data that was already sent stays in your Hypamoon project. The chat window and forms stay on your site until you turn the chat off or remove the form blocks; uninstalling the plugin removes them too.
sections.changelog:
1.5.0

  • New: the clean-move check, under Tools > Hypamoon, Clean-move check. Before Hypamoon moves your content, it looks for signs of a known break-in: Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 with the date of its files, the file wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php, the administrators, settings with program code in them, and scheduled tasks that stand out. It only reads; nothing is changed, removed or run. Only names, versions, dates and rule codes are sent to your Hypamoon project, never the content of a setting, a password or an email address. See Privacy and External services.
  • When the check finds something serious, your Hypamoon project pauses the move until the site is cleaned up. Nothing changes on your site.

1.4.2

  • Fix: Select all no longer silently replaces what your chat chose. When you send or save something that differs from the selection of your chat, the screen asks first (“Your chat selected only: Users. Send that, or send your own selection?”), with the choice of your chat as the default.
  • Log, security and analytics tables (Wordfence, BlogVault and BulletProof bv_ tables, MainWP Stream, Stream, iThemes Security, Sucuri, All In One WP Security, WP Cerber, Simple History, WP Activity Log, statistics plugins, and tables named like logs, sessions, transients or IP) are marked “Log or security data”. Tables with email or IP address columns are marked “Contains personal data”. Both are never ticked for you, also not with Select all and “Include personal data”, and Send asks for an extra yes when you tick one.
  • New: a signed wake route (POST /wp-json/hypamoon-connect/v1/wake). Right after you confirm sending in your chat, Hypamoon wakes the background check, so sending starts at once instead of within five minutes. The request carries no data and no token. See External services.
  • While a round runs, the background check keeps sending for up to two minutes, within the time limit of PHP, instead of 20 seconds.
  • The progress text says “Keep this page open to finish faster.” while a round runs.

1.4.1

  • Readme: the scheduled check of 1.4.0 is now described in the FAQ as well, and the license is written as GPLv2 or later. No change in what the plugin does.

1.4.0

  • New: your chat can suggest a selection. Move data shows “Your chat suggested a selection” with every kind of data, the reason, and what differs from your current selection. Apply suggestion ticks the boxes; personal data only with “Include personal data”. Then Save or Send as before. Dismiss removes it.
  • New: two modes. Simple, the default for a new installation, only connects and shows what was sent; your chat suggests, asks you to confirm and starts sending. Full is the screen you know, with every choice. Existing installations stay on Full after the update. Switching keeps your selection.
  • New: when your chat asks to send, the plugin starts the next time you open Tools > Hypamoon, or within about five minutes through a light WP-Cron check.
  • Tables and post types of other plugins that are rarely worth moving (cookie banners, importers, mail logs, search indexes, caches, logs) are marked “Usually not needed” and left out of Select all. You can still tick them one by one.
  • The message after sending is short: how much was sent, how many groups were skipped (details can be opened), and what to tell your chat next.

1.3.1

  • Fix: Select all no longer ticks Settings. Settings move only by name: tick the ones you want in the list under Show details. Names that look like a password, key, token, salt or auth setting are never offered.
  • Fix: a group that cannot move no longer stops the whole round. It is skipped with the reason, the rest is sent, and the end shows a summary like “Sent 483 of 483 items. Skipped: Settings (pick the settings you want by name first).”
  • Fix: the progress bar of an earlier round is no longer shown as if it were the current one. Send always saves your selection first and starts with a fresh bar.
  • The selected count counts settings per ticked name.

1.3.0

  • Tools > Hypamoon now has a tab per task: Connection, Move data, Site tools and Privacy, each with a short explanation at the top.
  • Move data groups your data (content, private post types, form entries, shop, users, database tables, settings) and shows per kind: the number of items, example fields with their type (text, number, date, relation, list), an estimated size, the last change, the collection it goes to in your project, and whether it holds personal data and why.
  • Show details lists all fields, the links that become references (like opdrachtgever_id to wp_users) and the filters.
  • Select all and Select none for the whole list, and a select all box per group. Personal data is left out of Select all unless you tick “Include personal data”. The selected count updates while you choose.
  • Nothing changes in what is sent or how: your connection and your selection stay as they are.

1.2.0

  • New: post types that are not public, like hours or applications of a member portal. Off until you choose them, and private.
  • New: “All fields” for content and users sends every other field too, and fields that point to a user or a post (like a client id) become links to those records.
  • New: database tables of plugins and themes, with their columns, in batches. Only when you choose a table; WordPress core tables are never offered.
  • New: settings from the options table, ticked one by one. Settings that look like a password, key or token are never listed or sent.
  • Users are sent before other data, so links to users resolve in the same round.
  • New filters: hypamoon_connect_private_post_types and hypamoon_connect_tables.

1.1.0

  • New: the chat window of your Hypamoon project on every page of your site, turned on from your chat with your AI assistant, your Hypamoon project or Tools > Hypamoon.
  • New: contact forms that send their entries to your Hypamoon project, with an email per entry, a bot check and a spam trap. Use the “Hypamoon form” block or the shortcode [hypamoon_form id="..."].
  • New: the filter hypamoon_connect_show_chat.
  • The chat and forms keep working when the access of the plugin expires.
  • The plugin never contacts Hypamoon while other admin pages load. On Tools > Hypamoon it loads the latest chat and form settings at most once every five minutes, with a short timeout.

1.0.2

  • Fix: the inventory was refused when a post type had no posts, so the selection could not be saved.
  • Saving the selection now shows the real reason when it fails, and only says it was changed elsewhere when that is true.

1.0.1

  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1.
  • Nonce checks directly in the handlers that read form data.
  • Safer database queries for WPForms entries and post statuses.
  • Uninstall also cleans up every site of a multisite network and the short-lived notices.

1.0.0

  • First release: connect with a one-time code, inventory, selection from chat, project or WordPress, batched export with resume, WP-CLI command.

The plugin stores its connection details in the WordPress options table, without autoload, and the chat and form settings in one small option, also without autoload. Uninstalling the plugin deletes them.

Terms: https://hypamoon.com/terms

External services

This plugin connects to the Hypamoon API (https://api.hypamoon.com), a service of Hypamoon, to move your data into your Hypamoon project.

  • When you press Connect, the one-time code, the site address, the site name, the WordPress version and the plugin version are sent, and an access token is received.
  • Right after connecting and when you press Refresh inventory, an overview of your site is sent: counts, dates, statuses, form field names, custom field definitions, the names of user fields and of meta fields of custom post types, the names and columns of database tables of plugins, and the names of settings (never their values), no content.
  • When you load or save the selection, the selection (which kinds of data, periods, statuses, fields to leave out, whether all fields go, and which settings) is read or written.
  • When you press Send or run wp hypamoon export, the data you selected is sent in batches.
  • When you press Disconnect, the access token is revoked.
  • When you open Move data, or the simple screen, the suggestion of your chat is read (which kinds of data, with a reason each) and whether your chat asked to send. When you apply and save it, or dismiss it, Hypamoon is told.
  • While the site is connected, WP-Cron checks every five minutes whether your chat asked to send your selection. If so, the selected data is sent in batches, for at most two minutes per check and always within the time limit of PHP. The check is removed when you disconnect or deactivate the plugin.
  • Wake route (since 1.4.2). Right after you confirm in your chat that your selection may be sent, Hypamoon (from api.hypamoon.com) sends a POST to https://your-site/?rest_route=/hypamoon-connect/v1/wake, so the check above runs at once instead of within five minutes. Why: without it, a site with few visitors can wait a long time for WP-Cron. The request holds no data and no token: only a timestamp, a random nonce and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over both, made with a key derived from the access token of your site. The plugin accepts it only with a valid signature, a clock at most five minutes apart and a nonce that was not used before, and at most 12 times per five minutes. It then plans the check (WP-Cron) and answers 202; the check itself sends only what you confirmed. If the route cannot be reached, nothing breaks: the five minute check picks the round up.
  • Clean-move check (since 1.5.0). Right after connecting, when you press Refresh inventory or Run the check, and at most every six hours during the five minute check, the result of the clean-move check is sent (see Privacy): versions, dates, logins with the domain of their email address, and names with rule codes. Never the content of a setting, a password or an email address.
  • When you open Tools > Hypamoon (at most once every five minutes), press Refresh, Turn chat on, Turn chat off or Set up forms, the chat and form settings for your site are read or changed: whether the chat is on, its colour, position, title and welcome text, the forms with their fields, and the public token of your project.

Every request from your WordPress server carries the access token and the address of your site. Apart from the five minute check above (or its wake), no request is made from your server without an action of an administrator, and none while other admin pages load.

The chat window and forms load scripts from the Hypamoon API in the browser of your visitors:

  • The chat window loads https://api.hypamoon.com/widget.js on every page while the chat is on. It reads the chat settings from Hypamoon, and sends the messages a visitor types to your Hypamoon project, where the assistant of your project answers.
  • A form loads https://api.hypamoon.com/form.js on the pages with a Hypamoon form. When a visitor sends the form, the fields are sent to your Hypamoon project.
  • Both show a bot check from Hypamoon in a small frame, which uses Cloudflare Turnstile. Cloudflare terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/ and privacy policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

These requests carry the public token of your project. It is public by design: it can only chat and add form entries, only from your site, with limits.
